payload.title: event_schema_field_drift and event_schema_required_drift ids are built from the contract path and event type only, so two catalogs registering one event type with drift emit two findings with the same id
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/event-contracts-adapter.ts:473 (id event-contracts:<contract path>:schema-field-drift:<eventType>, no schema file or variable)
tools/aria-adapters/event-contracts-adapter.ts:485 (the required-drift id has the same shape)
tools/aria-adapters/event-contracts-adapter.ts:430-444 (contracts are keyed by event type, so each schema entry for that type reaches the same single contract site)
tools/aria-adapters/event-contracts-adapter.ts:445-461 (every catalog entry is visited, so a second catalog with the same key produces a second finding)
payload.rule_violated: A finding id must identify one finding; the adapter output is consumed by id (ledger and judge dedupe), and the sibling nats test asserts that no id is emitted twice.
payload.notes: If a second typed catalog registers an event type that another catalog already registers (a plausible result of splitting a catalog file) and both have drift, the output holds two findings with one id and different evidence; an id-keyed consumer keeps one and the other drift is lost. On clean main there are 112 distinct catalog keys and no duplicate, so this is not reachable today. Close condition: Add the schema variable name (or schema file path) to both ids and add a scenario with two catalogs registering one drifted event type asserting two distinct ids. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 1). Verified at head a47dc4d57c of open pull request #2134; the cited code is not on main until that pull request merges.
